segments.text: «I say chethusurupasye annaathvanah, the individual being, for this individual being,
who has become one with mind, one with mind, that limited mind.
Mind that is soaked in the impressions of worldly pleasures, for him, Janam vandha, each
and every knowledge that he possesses is bondage, each and every knowledge.
It is not like the previous Sutra, Janam vandha, Janam vandha, there, it was the differentiated
knowledge was bondage and not knowing undifferentiated knowledge was also bondage.
But here, whatever knowledge he has, all knowledge is there differentiated, no question
of possessing undifferentiated knowledge there in this state.
Uku duku moho mai adeva saya ade vretruppam, the knowledge here that operates, operates
in three ways, three ways of action.
For instance, Nishchai, understanding, establishment of understanding and possessing ego, attaching
ego on that.
That is, the action of three organs, three intellectual organs, not cognitive organs or organs
of action.
These are three intellectual organs, by these intellectual organs, three actions are done.
First, understanding of whatever is to be enjoyed and then putting establishment on that
understanding, establishing that understanding, making it firm by intellect and third, attaching
your ego in it with it.
Which is, one with suk duku and moho, suk is connected with saadek state of life, duku
is connected with the rajas state of life and moho, illusio state is connected with tamasik
state of life.
And these three state of life are being operated by this ghana, by this ghana of individual
being.
Chitbe, ava, sanath, mukam, ghana, hence this kind of knowledge is only making you possess
the differentiated way of knowledge, differentiated knowledge, not undifferentiated knowledge at all.
That in reality is bonding, that tath bhandaha, tath bhajita, tath evi, I am samsaridhi.
Then he is entangled by these three ways of differentiated knowledge.
It is why he moves in various and repeated births and deaths in this world.
It is said in tantrasadbhava, sastra, sattastho, rajasasthascha, tamastho, guna vedaka, evam pari
atrthi aidehi, sthana, sthana, taramurajayat.
Sometimes situated in the state of sathik, ghun, sometimes situated in rajas and sometimes
situated in tamasik state of being.
Guna vedaka, in brief, in brief words he is residing in the perceptions of guna as one.
He is not beyond that.
He is not beyond the circle of guna.
He is sometimes situated in sathik state, sometimes in rajas state, sometimes in tamasik state.
It is why he pari atrthi, he moves in various births and deaths, sthana, sthana, taramurajayat.
He disconnects with previous state of life and united with the next state of life.
Disconnection means death and union means birth, then in another state of life.
This is narrated in spandha in these vanshalokandha.
Tanmatro dai rupeena manoham buddhivartina puriestakeena samrudas taduttham pratyodbhavam
bhunkte paravasho bhogam tadbhavat samsareth.
When tanmatras, five tanmatras give rise to the three intellectual organs, mind, ego and intellect.
Mind, ego and intellect rise from five tanmatras, shabhswar, shru, pras and gandh.
Collectively, these are eight organs, five tanmatras and three intellectual organs.
These are eight.
And this eight means is equal to puriestaka.
This is said to be puriestaka.
These eight function in our dreaming state.
When we go in dreaming state, these eight function there.
Shabhswar, shru, pras, gandh, these five tanmatras and mind, intellect and ego.
These eight only function there in dreaming state.
This is called puriestaka.
Collectively, these eight are called puriestaka.
And this puriestaka stops you in getting through the reality of your being state,
reality of your nature, reality of yourself.
Your reality of self is ignored by this puriestaka.
And when that is ignored, then what happens?
Tadvatam pratyodvam bhagam parvashav bhunkte.
So, he is, he dependently, he is not independent, he dependently enjoys the enjoyment therein.
Dependently, he can't, he can't put negation in this enjoyment.
He cannot cut that, he cannot refuse.
Tadvatam sarayat, by this he becomes pray, he becomes the footbar.
He is played by the wheel of repeated births and deaths.
So, he, he is entangled in the wheel of repeated births and deaths.
Adha samsrati praliyasya asya kauranam samprachakmahe.
Yet je dat pratyvidhana is pandasya asya.
And smantasya asya has in the end put the means of getting out of this puriestaka.
Adha, so samsrati praliyasya asya kauranam samprachakmahe.
Now, we'll put before you how this wheel of repeated births and deaths takes an end.
Thus, it is explained in smandasya asya.
